name: Swords and Republics: Wars of Greece and Rome
description: Heroes of Troy, the hoplites of Marathon, Alexander's phalanx and the legions of Rome, from the Bronze Age to the second century.

checkpoints.name: Bronze Age wars
checkpoints.note: Egyptian chariots clash at Kadesh, tradition tells of the siege of Troy, and around 1200 BCE palace states across the eastern Mediterranean collapse.

checkpoints.name: Greeks against Persia
checkpoints.note: The Persian Empire invades Greece. The Greeks win at Marathon, make a famous but losing stand at Thermopylae and win at sea at Salamis, and then Athens and Sparta turn on each other in the Peloponnesian War.

checkpoints.name: Alexander and his heirs
checkpoints.note: A Macedonian king beats Persia at Gaugamela and carries Greek culture to India. After his death his generals divide the empire in the Hellenistic period.

checkpoints.name: Rome against Carthage
checkpoints.note: Three wars with Carthage make Rome master of the western Mediterranean. Hannibal wins at Cannae but loses at Zama, and Carthage is destroyed in 146 BCE.

checkpoints.name: The Republic collapses
checkpoints.note: Slave revolt under Spartacus, Caesar's conquest of Gaul and his civil war show how armies come to decide Roman politics.

checkpoints.name: Empire and its borders
checkpoints.note: Octavian wins at Actium and rules as Augustus. The empire expands, loses legions in Germany, crushes revolts in Judea, and enjoys two centuries of order under the Pax Romana.
